newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian govt security prices steady in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Indian govt security prices steady in quiet trade.

text.p: Prices of Indian governemnt securities were steady in light noon trade Tuesday in a cautious market, dealers said.
They said it was not clear why trade was dull as call money had eased to 4.5-5.0 percent from last week's levels of above 9.0 percent.
"Normally when call eases, trade picks up," said a dealer at a foreign bank. "But today there are few buyers in the market."
He said one reason could be uncertainty over fund outflows from the banking system towards a repo auction to be held later in the day.

"Further there is also a rumour that there may be a fresh government bond issue in the near future," the dealer said. "Market players are speculating about a medium or long-term bond issue in the next few days as money market liquidity is good."
This could have made buyers cautious as a fresh isssue will drain funds away, he said.
In latest deals, the 12.59 percent 2004 stock was traded at 100.62 and 100.65 rupees, 13.40 percent 1999 at 105.35, 13.50 percent 1997 at 100.82 and the 12.14 percent 2000 at 102.03, dealers said.
